headNote: `head` names the commit this pass ran at - the last code commit before the evidence commits, cited as this rebase's replay of `d77fdb934` - and it cannot cite the commit it rides in with: a commit cannot name its own sha. This manifest is the MERGED record of two branches' evidence, re-derived for THIS head rather than carried from either side. It was synced twice inside one session because `main` moved twice: onto `73977340a` (`main`, 0.21.0, six commits past this branch's base `c0570ea60` - 0.20.0, 0.20.1, #139's New chat row, #140's Electron 44/TypeScript 7 toolchain and #128's mentioned-files and canvas rewrite), and then onto `7f0511dd4`, three more commits later (#147/#151's test-census and update-fixture fixes, and #153, which re-pointed `main`'s dangling provenance citations - two of them, `mentioned-files-app.capturedAtHead` and `partialCapture.addedAtHead`, onto the same commit this branch's own sync had chosen by hand, `e8ebe5c6d`: two independent fixes of one defect that agreed, and this manifest now carries `main`'s spelling of both). `main`'s declarations are carried through unchanged: its twenty `supplementary` sets (`mentioned-files-app` and `new-chat-row` among them) and the canvas pass's own addition record under `partialCapture` (`addedFrames` 12, `addedAtHead` `e8ebe5c6d`, with `addedAtHeadNote`, `provenanceNote` and `recaptureNote` untouched) - while every count is counted off the merged tree instead of added from either side: 1154 `.webp` are committed, the 20 sets declare 150, leaving `frames` 1004; `surfaces` 130 is `capture-evidence.mjs`'s `STORIES.length` at this head; `themes` stays 12 - and `head`, `srcTree` and `scriptsTree` are this head's, which is the equality the gate asserts against `HEAD:src`/`HEAD:scripts` at the commit that carries these frames. `capturedAt` is still the last full SWEEP's stamp, and that is what it labels: the counts describe the swept set, not this branch's narrowed pass. The frames this branch contributes were RE-TAKEN at the head above (see `partialCapture`) because `main` moved a file inside their import closure - `src/shared/desktop-contract.ts`, changed by `e8ebe5c6d` (#128) - so the claim that they are pictures of this source rests on a run rather than on an argument. The other 37 files `main` touched under `src/` are outside that closure, checked against esbuild's metafile for `slash-commands.stories.tsx` (50 modules in the closure, 1 of `main`'s 38 changed `src` files inside it; the one that is inside adds exported constants and types only). `dirtyWorkingTree` is true and it is not the frames' code: exactly one file was uncommitted when the capture ran, `.storybook/main.ts`, with `typescript.reactDocgen` turned off, because `react-docgen-typescript@2.2.2` throws at module load against the TypeScript 7.0.2 the committed lockfile installs (`ts.JsxEmit` is undefined in TS 7, so its `lib/parser.js:31` reads `React` off nothing) and Storybook's preview build dies before a story is served - #140's toolchain move broke Storybook repo-wide, and no CI job builds Storybook, so nothing caught it. Docgen extracts props metadata for the docs and args panels and paints no pixel; with that one flag off the frames still come from the project's own config, aliases and Tailwind scan, which is checked rather than asserted: the served CSS carries the same 1162 selectors and the composer stand-in's `h-11` resolves to the 44px the committed frames show. One trap is recorded here for the next reader, because it cost a whole pass: a first re-take came back with every one of the 180 frames 22px off the committed geometry, and the stylesheet it had been served was generated from a different project (`.h-11` absent, and 34 selectors short of the committed sheet). Two causes look identical from outside - a Storybook `--config-dir` outside the repository root, whose Tailwind scan then roots in the wrong project, and the fact that port 6061 is shared with a sibling session's Storybook on this host - so the re-take that is on disk was accepted on measured server identity rather than on the flags it was launched with: the sheet it served carried the same 1162 selectors, `h-11` resolved to the committed 44px, and the story geometry matched the committed frames.

countsMean.frames: The sweep's own frame count, asserted by `check-evidence.mjs` against the frames on disk that fall outside any declared `supplementary` set - 1004 at this head, and the assertion is the definition rather than a restatement of it: 1154 `.webp` are committed and the 20 `supplementary` sets below account for 150 of them (one of those sets declares no frames), leaving 1004. Re-derived for THIS tree and stated once, after the two rebases onto `main` (`73977340a`, then `7f0511dd4`): the two sides had each written their own figure and neither survives as such, because the merged tree is the UNION of both frame sets - 974 `.webp` on `main` (824 swept plus the 150 its sets declare) plus this branch's 180 `chat-slash-completion` frames, the only frames it adds, 1154 in all (its other 870 swept frames are `main`'s own, carried from the base this branch was cut from) - so the figure is counted off the disk and the summed declared frames rather than added from either side's field. Superseded derivations are deleted rather than quoted, on the rule this field already carried: a stale derivation is worse here than none, because the field's whole justification is that a reader can re-compute it, and one that does not resolve teaches them to stop checking. The three terms above are the whole arithmetic, they are read from the tree rather than transcribed (`find docs/evidence -name '*.webp' | wc -l`, and the summed `frames` of the sets below), and `check-evidence.mjs` fails when they disagree with it. This branch carries no version bump of its own: it is rebased rather than merged with a bump, so `package.json` on it reads the base's `0.21.0` and no resolution along the way touched the version line.
countsMean.surfaces: `capture-evidence.mjs`'s `STORIES.length` at the head above - 130 entries, counted off the merged literal by the gate itself rather than summed from the two sides: 115 on `main` at `7f0511dd4` plus the fifteen `chat-slash-completion` stories this branch registers that `main` does not (command-phase, -narrowed, -fuzzy and -scrolled, argument-phase-teams, -no-match, -models, -empty, -narrow-composer, -themes, -loading-and-error and -truncating-name, inline-mid-draft, name-list-completed). The gate counts the list and fails a mismatch, so this field cannot silently lag its own source.

partialCapture.note: RE-CAPTURE at the head above, and the pass THIS record describes: the fifteen `chat-slash-completion` stories at twelve themes each, 180 frames, all written at `29c757995`. All 180 came back BYTE-IDENTICAL to the bytes already committed - that is the pass's result, not a reason it was not needed, and it held on both syncs, so the same 180 files are pictured at three heads. The re-take was forced by the rebase: `main` moved a module inside these stories' import closure (`src/shared/desktop-contract.ts`, `e8ebe5c6d`, additive exports only), so 'these are pictures of this source' could not stay an argument about a subtree; 180/180 identical bytes is the strongest available answer to it, and it says the closure change is inert in pixels while the other 37 files `main` touched under `src/` are outside the closure at all. The capture ran with `typescript.reactDocgen` off and against the operator's live backend (`--allow-backend`, the narrowed-run flag), both recorded in `headNote`: the first because Storybook cannot build otherwise on TypeScript 7, the second because the operator's own app owns port 1111. The backend question is settled in the bytes rather than argued - a live backend answering at the configured URL still produced the same 180 frames the offline set holds - and the docgen question is settled in the CSS (same selectors, `h-11` resolving to its committed 44px). The `added*` fields above, `addedAtHeadNote`, `provenanceNote` and `recaptureNote` are `main`'s records of its own passes, carried through unchanged because the frames they describe are on disk untouched; the `refreshed*` fields are THIS pass's, and they necessarily supersede `main`'s own refresh record of the canvas surfaces, because the field can only hold the latest pass.
partialCapture.provenanceNote:
THE REBASE, and the first one here that re-stamps without re-capturing. `main` moved three times under this branch during the round - to `e4d074c60` (0.19.6), to `98c32e85e` (0.19.7 plus #138, which the previous pass re-captured at), and then to `c0570ea60` (0.19.7 plus #136). That move is not packaging: it adds `src/renderer/src/features/chat/clear-search.ts` and rewrites the search field in `src/renderer/src/features/chat/components/chat-sidebar.tsx` (+51/-8), so `srcTree` moved for the first time in any of these rebases, and `scripts/` moved with it (`scripts/clear-search.test.mjs`). A stamp whose tree has moved is exactly the case the earlier passes answered by re-capturing; this one answered it with two facts about the frames. The first is the shape of the change: it paints a clear control INSIDE the field and only while the query is non-empty (the `{query && ...}` guard around the button in `chat-sidebar.tsx`), plus a `pr-9` on the input that reserves the control's column and a `my-2` moved from the input onto a `relative` wrapper around it, which reproduces the same box - so with an empty query the field renders the same placeholder, the same border and the same box as it did before. The second is the measurement that closes it: `clear-search/before-rest` and `clear-search/after-rest` are BYTE-IDENTICAL in both themes, the same empty-query sidebar painted once on the pre-change tree and once on the post-change tree, so nothing in that state depends on #136 at all. Every frame in this tree of that state is therefore unchanged, and the only frames whose state differs are the non-empty-query ones, all of them in `clear-search` itself, which were taken on the changed tree by #136. The sets that carry the field besides `clear-search` were looked at rather than assumed to be empty: `chat-title` and `sidebar-new-chat` draw the empty placeholder with no clear control in all 38 of their frames across both themes, `model-picker-feedback` shows the same empty field behind its scrim, and `mentioned-files-app` is cropped to the canvas panel's own measured rect and carries no sidebar at all; no other set in the tree is about that field - `clear-search`'s own README and readbacks are the only evidence in the tree that names it. Nothing else in the tree was a different source for these pixels either, and that is measurable in the same way: 0 `.webp` differ between the head the previous pass ran at (`98b827108`, orphaned by the force-push that carried this re-stamp) and this head.

THE SYNC MERGE, and what it does and does not claim about the frames. `main` moved three times more - to `6f9bc2d04` (#140: the desktop toolchain, Electron 44 and TypeScript 7), to `4ffc3f2b5` (#139: the New chat row aligned with All chats, without the pill) and to `ad09ec6b4` (the 0.20.1 release) - and this branch was merged up onto it rather than replayed onto it, because a rebase would rewrite all twenty-two commits and orphan every citation this manifest carries while changing no pixel a reader can see. Two paths conflicted: `package.json` (resolved the same way as before - `main`'s `version` line, now 0.20.1, with the UNION of the two sides' `test:desktop` lists, which now carry all three of the test files the sides added, this branch's `mentioned-files.test.mjs` and `main`'s `new-chat-row.test.mjs` and `new-chat-row-evidence.test.mjs`) and this manifest's stamp block, where two re-stamps had to be reconciled; `src/main/index.ts` was auto-merged, both sides' hunks kept. No frame was re-taken for the merge, and the two upstream changes are treated differently for a reason. #140 moves the toolchain (`package.json`, `electron.vite.config.js`, the `tsconfig`s, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, three `scripts/` files, five `src/main/` modules and one renderer component) and not the canvas, the mentioned-files producer or the sidebar, and `main` itself did not re-sweep for it: it re-stamped its trees and committed the toolchain set's own packaged frame beside the swept ones, which is the same position this branch takes for the frames it contributed. #139 does move the sidebar's New chat row, and the three sets that photograph the sidebar (`chat-title`, `sidebar-new-chat` and `model-picker-feedback`'s scrimmed background) predate it: they are pictures of the sidebar as it stood at the heads their `capturedAtHead` fields name, this manifest makes no claim that they show the post-#139 row, and `main` carries that change's own before/after evidence beside them in the `new-chat-row` set - which is why the merge adds that set rather than re-driving those older frames. Nothing on either side of the merge touches this branch's own contribution: the canvas surfaces and `mentioned-files-app` are cropped to panels that #139 and #140 do not paint.
partialCapture.addedNote: `addedAt`/`addedAtHead` above are the ROUND-2 pass's: they record the last pass that added a surface (`canvas-workspace/files-scan-stopped-empty`, twelve frames, at the replay of the head it ran on), so `addedFrames` 12 and `addedSurfaces` name that pass and not the re-capture that re-stamped it. The distinction is R3-1's: the pass that wrote `refreshedFrames: 48` counted the ADDED story's twelve frames in a number a reader reads as `re-captured in place`, so the two figures were conflated. Round 4 (R4-1) found the pair could not be trusted at all - a re-stamp overwrote `addedAt`/`addedAtHead` with its own run while resetting `addedFrames` to 0 and `addedSurfaces` to `[]`, so the fields named a pass that had added nothing and could not be fetched. `partialAddedFields` in `capture-evidence.mjs` now decides the citation (covered by `evidence-manifest.test.mjs`) and `check-evidence.mjs` holds both head citations to the reachability bar it applies to `head`. This rebase's re-capture found the COUNTS half of the same rule still open - it is a zero-add pass, and `main`'s accumulating writer reset them to 0/[] anyway, which is what these two values were corrected from - so the writer now leaves the whole added-pass record alone unless a run actually adds frames. Both rebase passes since are zero-add passes and the writer left that record alone, which is the corrected behaviour: `addedFrames` 12 and `addedSurfaces` still name the round-2 pass, and only the citation above moves, each time to the new rebase's replay of the same commit.

unchangedControl.why: The honesty check for this pass, and the reason a moved frame is legible as one: a surface this rebase does not paint differently was re-captured through the same command, on the same host, in the same session as the nine it does. All twelve came back BYTE-IDENTICAL, so the encoder and the renderer are deterministic here at this load. The class the moved frames belong to was measured the same way in the previous pass, which ran `audio-viewer` twice: its `neon` frame - which moved in the first run of BOTH passes - came back exactly the committed bytes in that second run. Neither control separates the widget from the encoder for `pdf-viewer/localOperatorDark`, whose difference is the platform PDF plugin not painting at all and which reproduced byte-for-byte instead (see `recaptureNote`).

partialCapture.recaptureNote: Re-captured in place, at the rebased head, and the result is one-sided: 101 of the 108 frames came back BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed bytes, and all 48 of the four Files surfaces plus all 12 control frames are among them. The 7 that moved are media-viewer frames - pdf 1 (`localOperatorDark`), image 2 (`synth`, `radient`), audio 2 (`neon`, `radient`), video 2 (`synth`, `radient`) - and six of the seven moved only at the lossy encoder's own quantisation scale: at an 8% tolerance (20/255) ZERO pixels differ, and the worst RMSE is 0.00054 (`video-viewer/radient`, 4,342 px of 1,152,000). That class is established rather than assumed: the same command on the same tree was run twice in the previous pass, and `audio-viewer/neon` - which moved in both passes' first runs - came back EXACTLY the committed bytes in one of them, so the movement is the widget repaint and the encoder and a frame that has moved is not read as a change unless it survives a second run. The seventh, `pdf-viewer/localOperatorDark`, is a reproducible platform paint failure and not that class: this session's private headless Chrome never painted the PDF guest document - a probe at 640,200 reads the platform field `srgb(40,40,40)` where the committed frame reads the white page - with a byte-for-byte identical difference (204,364 px, 163,673 of them above 8%) in both passes. The viewer's own source (`pdf-preview.tsx`, `canvas-file-viewer.tsx`, the story) is untouched by `main`'s move, and this branch's canvas hunks in `chat-page.tsx` and `chat-content.tsx` - the one host surface the rebase had to carry - survive line-for-line, so the committed frame is the one that depicts the surface under review; it is retained and NO byte-identity claim is made for it. The 7 frames whose committed bytes are retained are the same picture the re-capture measured.
partialCapture.addedAtHeadNote: This is the pass that ADDED the twelve `canvas-workspace--files-scan-stopped-empty` frames, cited as the replay of the head it ran on: the original `58d3dfc05` is no longer reachable from any ref after an earlier force-push, its replay `46684b07e` was orphaned by the rebase onto 0.19.6, that replay's replay `5d2a04778` was orphaned by the rebase onto `fb9c0942e`, its next replay `9bf8a6357` was orphaned by the rebase onto `98c32e85e`, and its last one `a32475ed5` was orphaned in turn by the rebase onto `c0570ea60` - so the citation is this rebase's replay, `a9ed72ad7`. These pairs are not range-diff `=` where they differ at all: their patches differ in this rebase's spelling of the manifest alone, because that file's prose and counters were re-based on the new `main` on both sides, so every frame and every source path that commit carries is the same one, which is the property a citation is for. The twelve frames themselves were committed by `49442eaec`, this branch's reachable replay of the commit that carried them (its pre-rebase spelling was `19bfea347`), which is where a reader who wants the tree they landed in should look.

The panel frame shows the producer firing over a real transcript: six inferred paths become six tiles under the head, with the ghost carrying the `No longer on disk` receipt and the video tile painting a real frame.
